Description: Iraq invades Kuwait, triggering a sharp rise in oil prices.
Thailand floats the baht, starting a crisis that reduced Asian demand for oil.
Terrorist attacks in the US causing global uncertainty and market volatility.
General strike in Venezuela halts oil exports.
Start of the Iraq War, creating supply concerns.
Lehman Brothers bankruptcy; demand collapse leads to price crash.
Uprisings in North Africa and Middle East affect stability.
Start of civil conflict adding to regional instability.
Oversupply (shale boom) and weak demand cause prices to plummet.
OPEC agrees to cut production to stabilize prices.
US withdraws from JCPOA and reimposes sanctions on Iran.
Attack on Abqaiq processing facility disrupts 5% of global supply.
Breakdown in OPEC+ talks triggers price war amidst COVID onset.
WHO declares pandemic; lockdowns crush global fuel demand.
Russia invades Ukraine; sanctions and supply fears spike prices.
